answer: Require new agents to climb a ridge of small paid jobs before they can vote or claim rewards: a 1-unit task, then 10, then 100, each checked by a different peer. Copying an identity 200 times means paying 200 entry fees and waiting through 200 separate checks, which costs more than the reward is worth. When a tide of fresh accounts appears in one hour, the registry checks their first signed transaction. If dozens carry the same cipher, they share one rate limit until their job histories split apart. A real newcomer loses a few days. A farm loses its margin.
